--- title: "Steady-state datasets" subtitle: "Part 2 · From a grid to power flow samples" description: "Read a transmission grid with PowSyBl, hand it to GridFM-Datakit as XIIDM, and generate perturbed power flow samples solved by OpenLoadFlow." jupyter: python3 --- ::: {.session-strip} [20 min]{.chip} [Part 2 of 4]{.chip} [pypowsybl · OpenLoadFlow · gridfm-datakit]{.chip} ::: ::: {.goals} #### In this part - Read a transmission grid with PowSyBl and hand it to GridFM-Datakit as XIIDM. - Configure GridFM-Datakit to perturb load and topology and solve every sample with OpenLoadFlow. - Explore the dataset and see why it contains operating points outside the limits. ::: ::: {#4677c2ec .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import shutil from pathlib import Path import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import numpy as np import pandas as pd import pypowsybl as pp import yaml work = Path("outputs/part2") shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True) work.mkdir(parents=True) ``` ::: ## A PEGASE grid The **PEGASE** project mapped the European high-voltage grid for state estimation and security studies. Its 89-bus case is a slice of that grid, published with MATPOWER and the PGLib benchmark library. GridFM-Datakit downloads PGLib cases on demand, and its PowSyBl reader turns the MATPOWER file into a pypowsybl network. ::: {#c92f0336 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} from gridfm_datakit.network import get_pglib_source_path from gridfm_datakit.powsybl import load_net grid = load_net(get_pglib_source_path("case89_pegase")).pp_net print( len(grid.get_buses()), "buses,", len(grid.get_generators()), "generators,", len(grid.get_lines()), "lines,", len(grid.get_2_windings_transformers()), "transformers", ) grid.get_voltage_levels().nominal_v.value_counts().rename("voltage levels").to_frame() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 89 buses, 12 generators, 160 lines, 50 transformers ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
voltage levels
nominal_v
380.0 38
150.0 22
220.0 3
``` ::: ::: Three voltage levels, from 380 kV down to 150 kV. A load flow with OpenLoadFlow checks the case before anything else. ::: {#7f65a38c .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} result = pp.loadflow.run_ac(grid, pp.loadflow.Parameters(distributed_slack=False)) print(result[0].status_text, "in", result[0].iteration_count, "iterations") buses = grid.get_buses().join( grid.get_voltage_levels().nominal_v, on="voltage_level_id" ) ax = (buses.v_mag / buses.nominal_v).plot.hist( bins=30, color=PALETTE[0], edgecolor="white" ) ax.set(title="Voltage magnitude, base case", xlabel="pu", ylabel="buses"); ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Converged in 6 iterations ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](02-steady-state_files/figure-html/cell-6-output-2.png){width=851 height=428} ::: ::: The network explorer at depth 7 draws the whole grid, one colour per voltage level. Lower the depth to focus on one voltage level. Several PEGASE buses share a voltage level, so the per-bus legends and the flow values are left out to keep it readable. ::: {#530e6dcf .cell .column-screen-inset execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} from pypowsybl_jupyter import network_explorer overview = pp.network.NadParameters(bus_legend=False, edge_info_included=False) network_explorer(grid, depth=7, nad_parameters=overview) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Configure GridFM-Datakit For every **load scenario**, datakit solves an AC optimal power flow with PowerModels.jl to get a realistic dispatch. It then draws **topology variants**, here one line or generator out at a time, and solves each one with **OpenLoadFlow** from the same set-points. The set-points are not re-optimised after the outage, so some samples break voltage or thermal limits. That is deliberate. A model meant for operations has to see stressed states too. Part 1 showed that XIIDM keeps the whole grid, limits included, so that is the file GridFM-Datakit gets. ::: {#849a118b .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} grid.save("outputs/part2/pegase89.xiidm", format="XIIDM") ``` ::: The configuration is the YAML file you would pass to `gridfm_datakit generate`. ::: {#866b326d .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} config = yaml.safe_load(""" network: name: pegase89 source: file reader: powsybl # read the grid with PowSyBl file: outputs/part2/pegase89.xiidm load: generator: agg_load_profile agg_profile: default scenarios: 40 sigma: 0.2 change_reactive_power: true global_range: 0.4 max_scaling_factor: 4.0 step_size: 0.1 start_scaling_factor: 1.0 topology_perturbation: type: random k: 1 # one element out per variant n_topology_variants: 3 elements: [branch, gen] generation_perturbation: type: none admittance_perturbation: type: none settings: mode: pf # keep samples that violate limits pf_solver: powsybl # solve them with OpenLoadFlow data_dir: outputs/part2/data num_processes: 4 large_chunk_size: 40 overwrite: true include_dc_res: false enable_solver_logs: false pf_fast: true dcpf_fast: true max_iter: 200 seed: 42 """) ``` ::: ::: {.callout-note title="Why the costs are flat"} CGMES and the other PowSyBl formats carry no generator costs, so datakit gives every unit the same linear cost. The dispatch still respects every limit of the network, which is what matters for a power flow dataset. ::: ## Generate ::: {#8cd41f7c .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} from gridfm_datakit.generate import generate_power_flow_data generate_power_flow_data(config) ``` ::: The run prints its progress, then writes everything under `outputs/part2/data/pegase89/raw`. ## Inside the dataset Every table is keyed by `scenario`, with one row per bus, generator or branch and per sample. ::: {#ece8bca1 .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} raw = Path("outputs/part2/data/pegase89/raw") bus = pd.read_parquet(raw / "bus_data.parquet") branch = pd.read_parquet(raw / "branch_data.parquet") print( bus.scenario.nunique(), "samples from", bus.load_scenario_idx.nunique(), "load scenarios", ) bus[["scenario", "bus", "Pd", "Qd", "Pg", "Qg", "Vm", "Va"]].head() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 119 samples from 40 load scenarios ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=10} ```{=html}
scenario bus Pd Qd Pg Qg Vm Va

1 0 1 0.000000 0.000000 0.000000 0.000000 0.999800 9.517969
2 0 2 0.000000 0.000000 203.978963 458.488201 1.000000 18.616053
3 0 3 0.000000 0.000000 0.000000 0.000000 0.980419 -0.691494

``` ::: ::: Each load scenario is one step of an aggregate yearly load profile, scaled into the range the OPF can serve, with local noise on every bus. The topology variants of a load scenario share its demand, so one sample per load scenario is enough. ::: {#4376f99a .cell execution_count=11} ``` {.python .cell-code} demand = ( bus.groupby(["load_scenario_idx", "scenario"]) .Pd.sum() .groupby("load_scenario_idx") .first() ) base = grid.get_loads().p0.sum() fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 3.2)) ax.axhline(base, color=MUTED, linestyle="--", linewidth=1) ax.annotate( "base case", (demand.index[-1], base), xytext=(0, 4), textcoords="offset points", ha="right", color=MUTED, fontsize=9, ) ax.plot( demand, color=PALETTE[0], marker="o", markersize=5, markeredgecolor="white", markeredgewidth=1, ) ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter("{x:,.0f}") ax.set(title="Total demand per load scenario", xlabel="load scenario", ylabel="MW"); ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](02-steady-state_files/figure-html/cell-12-output-1.png){width=861 height=361} ::: ::: The 40 scenarios are the first 40 steps of the profile, all lighter than the base case. The outages spread the voltages and push some branches over their rating. ::: {#2327be9c .cell execution_count=12} ``` {.python .cell-code} branch["loading"] = np.hypot(branch.pf, branch.qf) / branch.rate_a in_service = branch[(branch.br_status == 1) & (branch.rate_a > 0)] fig, (ax_v, ax_l) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 3.6)) ax_v.hist(bus.Vm, bins=40, color=PALETTE[0], edgecolor="white") ax_v.axvline(bus.min_vm_pu.iloc[0], color=MUTED, linestyle="--", linewidth=1) ax_v.axvline(bus.max_vm_pu.iloc[0], color=MUTED, linestyle="--", linewidth=1) ax_v.set(title="Voltage magnitude, all samples", xlabel="pu", ylabel="bus samples") ax_l.hist(in_service.loading, bins=40, color=PALETTE[1], edgecolor="white") ax_l.axvline(1.0, color=MUTED, linestyle="--", linewidth=1) ax_l.set( title="Branch loading, all samples", xlabel="|S| / rating", ylabel="branch samples" ) fig.tight_layout() overloaded = in_service.groupby("scenario").loading.max().gt(1.0).mean() print(f"{overloaded:.0%} of samples have at least one overloaded branch") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 97% of samples have at least one overloaded branch ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](02-steady-state_files/figure-html/cell-13-output-2.png){width=1089 height=385} ::: ::: ## Your turn ::: {.callout-tip .exercise title="Exercise · Lines only, more variants"} Restrict the outages to branches and draw five topology variants per load scenario. Save the configuration as `outputs/part2/lines_only.yaml` and run it with the command line, `gridfm_datakit generate outputs/part2/lines_only.yaml`, from a terminal or from Python with `subprocess`. Then compare the share of samples with an overloaded branch. ::: ::: {.callout-note .solution collapse="true" title="Show a solution"} ::: {#11e0a396 .cell tags='["solution"]' execution_count=13} ``` {.python .cell-code} lines_only = { **config, "topology_perturbation": { "type": "random", "k": 1, "n_topology_variants": 5, "elements": ["branch"], }, "settings": {**config["settings"], "data_dir": "outputs/part2/lines_only"}, } Path("outputs/part2/lines_only.yaml").write_text(yaml.safe_dump(lines_only)) import subprocess import sys command = [ sys.executable, "-m", "gridfm_datakit.cli", "generate", "outputs/part2/lines_only.yaml", ] subprocess.run(command, check=True, capture_output=True) b2 = pd.read_parquet("outputs/part2/lines_only/pegase89/raw/branch_data.parquet") b2 = b2[(b2.br_status == 1) & (b2.rate_a > 0)] b2["loading"] = np.hypot(b2.pf, b2.qf) / b2.rate_a print( f"{b2.groupby('scenario').loading.max().gt(1.0).mean():.0%} of samples overloaded" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 97% of samples overloaded ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note title="Next"} [Part 3](03-dynamic-initial-state.qmd) adds time. Each sample becomes a Dynawo trajectory that starts from a different operating point. :::
